text:
maria: Quick heads-up — ran a comparison between the new kernel-selector (v2) and baseline for the paired-model apples test. p95 latency regressed ~12% when KV-cache hits > 40%.

kevin_h: ugh. Is that on replay or synthetic?

maria: replay harness. Same prompts, same decode params, same stop sequences. I replayed last week's traffic slice (10k requests) through both runtimes.

leah: did you force tokenizer alignment? We saw one weird tokenization mismatch cause different prefix lengths and K cache sizes earlier.

maria: yes — tokenizer checksum step included. I validated tokens are identical for 99.99% of requests. Only 3 mismatches, none of which correlated to the regressions.

samir: can you paste the run command & key metrics?

maria: sure — run commands and a short log:

```
./harness/replay --model redwood-open-13b --decode "temp=0.2,top_p=0.95,stop=\"\n\"" --tokenizer-checksum --kernel-selector=v2 --out=run_v2.json
./harness/replay --model redwood-open-13b --decode "temp=0.2,top_p=0.95,stop=\"\n\"" --tokenizer-checksum --kernel-selector=baseline --out=run_base.json
```

Summary (10k reqs each):
- baseline p50/p95/p99: 45ms / 128ms / 340ms
- v2 p50/p95/p99: 48ms / 143ms / 360ms
- error rate: both ~0.1% (same errors)
- throughput: v2 dropped ~6% under sustained 2k RPS

kevin_h: hmmm kernel selection sounds like it's choosing a slower kernel for some shapes when KV hit ratio is high. Could be batching heuristics + warmup interaction.

leah: did you capture GPU utilization / SM stalls / memory bandwidth?

maria: I have a short perf dump attached in run_v2.prof. Key notes: higher CPI, and a larger fraction of time in attention kernel for some batches.

samir: probably the runtime is picking the fused attention kernel for short sequences but then KV cache changes sequence-length distribution mid-request. We should try forcing kernel to baseline implementation to confirm.

maria: I re-ran with `--force-kernel=baseline-attn` and p95 matched baseline. So selector is the likely culprit.

ajacobs: nice repro. Next steps: 1) add a unit in kernel-selector tests to freeze on traces with high KV-hit ratios; 2) run paired synthetic run to narrow down if replay specifics (prefix pattern) matter; 3) open perf regression ticket with the profiler dump.

leah: for the synthetic run, try synthetic prefix distribution that mirrors real replay: variable-length prefixes drawn from the empirical histogram (0, 8, 32, 128). When KV cache warmup is mismatched the batching pipeline behaves differently.

maria: will do. quick question — should we also align stop-seq handling? The runtime has a fast-path for stop checks during decode which differs between kernels. Could that explain the p99 tail?

kevin_h: yes include exact stop sequences in synthetic payloads, and run with `--stop-check=sync` to force the same code path. Also disable optimistic early-exit optimizations for parity.

maria: noted. I'll post new numbers.

(15m later)

maria: synthetic run with matching prefix histogram + `--force-stop-sync` + same decode params: p95 delta reduced to ~3% and throughput gap disappears. So it's an interaction: kernel-selector picks a kernel that assumes cheap stop-checks; with replay the stop-checks hit a different path making it slower.

samir: perfect isolate. That means two fixes: 1) selector should consider stop-check-cost estimate per-kernel; 2) add an automated apples-to-apples test that runs both replay and synthetic variants and compares latency/throughput.

ajacobs: I've created PERF-1422 with the profiler artifacts and initial mitigations (selector fallback policy when KV-hit > 30% or stop-cost > threshold).

maria: thanks. I'll add the synthetic harness config to the repo under `harness/configs/token-sync-hist.json` and a short reproducer script in `harness/scripts/repro_selector_regression.sh`.

leah: can someone add an entry to the regression dashboard? We should alert on p95 shift > 5% after kernel-selector changes.

kevin_h: i'll wire an alert. Also let's add a tiny unit test that runs a micro-replay (100 reqs) under CI with kernel-selector toggled — should catch obvious regressions quickly.

maria: putting PR together now. tl;dr: regression is real but reproducible; interaction between kernel-selection heuristic and stop-check path under realistic KV-hit distributions. Patch will include selector telemetry to explain future decisions. :thumbsup:
